Optimized selectivity in CO2 electrochemical reduction using amorphous CuNi catalysts: Insights from density functional theory and machine learning simulations
abstract: Amorphous materials represent a promising platform for advancing CO 2 electrochemical reduction due to their inherently diverse coordination environments. In this study, we demonstrate computationally the superior performance of amorphous CuNi alloys for CO 2 electrochemical reduction. By integrating machine learning forcefields for efficient structure generation and density functional theory for subsequent structural refinement and property calculations, we reveal the potential of these disordered systems to outperform their crystalline counterparts. Machine learning forcefields can generate a bulk structure containing a mixture of Cu and Ni atoms, resulting in enhanced catalytic performance. Effective screening of the amorphous surfaces is used to identify undercoordinated Cu and Ni sites in the amorphous structure to synergistically promote selective CO production and favor ethanol formation over ethylene via the stabilization of the *COCHO intermediate, resulting in significantly lower Gibbs free energy changes compared to the crystalline counterpart. The varying atomic coordination environments on amorphous surfaces promote both C–C bond formation and subsequent proton-electron transfer, leading to ethanol formation. These findings demonstrate the superior catalytic performance of amorphous CuNi, highlighting its potential for efficient and selective electroreduction of CO 2 .

Towards artificial intelligence-enabled autonomous battery prognostics and management
abstract: Reliable and safe operation of batteries is increasingly challenged by diverse operating conditions and stringent demands for system resilience. Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative enabler of battery health management, offering capabilities beyond traditional models. This review provides a structured synthesis of recent progress in AI-enabled diagnostics. Advances in state estimation—including state of health (SOH) and remaining useful life (RUL)—are first examined, with methodological breakthroughs identified across diverse task formulations. The evolution of AI architectures is then traced, from conventional neural networks to attention-based Transformers, physics-informed models, and federated learning, with particular attention to emerging paradigms such as foundation models, neuro-symbolic reasoning, and quantum machine learning that promise improved robustness and interpretability. To bridge laboratory innovation with deployment, a domain-adaptive four-stage data pipeline has emerged as a promising framework for real-world BMS signals—spanning operational segmentation, multi-scale denoising, degradation-aware feature engineering, and structured sample construction—designed to enhance generalization under heterogeneous and noisy conditions. Looking forward, a technological roadmap is outlined that integrates edge AI, digital twins, AIOps, quantum computing, wireless sensing, and self-repair systems. Collectively, these innovations transform batteries from passive energy reservoirs into intelligent cyber-physical agents endowed with perception, autonomous decision-making, and resilient fault response—paving the way toward truly battery-centric autonomous energy systems.

title: AI-augmented electrochemical model for lithium-ion battery: Recent advances and perspectives
Machine learning predicts microstructure impact on discharge performance in hard carbon anodes for K-ion batteries
Large language models for battery prognostics
abstract: Predicting battery health with accuracy and interpretability has become a grand challenge at the intersection of electrochemistry, artificial intelligence, and sustainable energy. Conventional data-driven and physics-based methods remain constrained by nonlinear, coupled, and heterogeneous battery dynamics that limit generalization across chemistries, duty cycles, and environments. Recent breakthroughs in large language models (LLMs) and foundation-model artificial intelligence introduce a paradigm shift—enabling machines to learn from multimodal signals, encode physical laws, and reason adaptively across scales. This review unifies these advances into ten foundational methodologies that delineate the emerging landscape of intelligent battery prognostics: transfer learning, knowledge augmentation, physics-informed and explainable intelligence, ensemble fusion, causal reasoning, continual adaptation, multi-agent coordination, digital-twin coupling, and the pursuit of artificial general intelligence. Together, these dimensions redefine batteries from passive electrochemical devices into cognitive energy systems—self-optimizing, trustworthy, and responsive to uncertainty. Framed within the broader evolution toward Industry 5.0, we chart a roadmap for autonomous battery management that fuses physics, data, and reasoning, establishing artificial intelligence as a scientific and technological cornerstone for the next generation of resilient, adaptive, and sustainable electrification.

Assembling atomically dispersed tungsten co-catalysts on organometal halide perovskite for superior interfacial charge transfer and photocatalytic hydrogen production
abstract: Intensifying the electronic metal-support interaction (EMSI) between organometal halide perovskites (OMHPs) photocatalysts and hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) co-catalyst is crucial for realizing efficient interfacial charge transfer and solar-to-hydrogen (STH) conversion. Although atomically dispersed catalysts (ADCs) are prone to form stronger EMSI than nanoparticles with support, assembling ADCs on OMHPs remains a great challenge due to the ionic nature and thermal instability of OMHPs. Herein, we realize the design of two-dimensional (2D) OMHP PMA2PbI4 (PMA = C6H5(CH2)NH3+) loaded with nonnoble metal-based ADCs, namely tungsten ADCs (WADCs), for the first time. We show that WADCs coordinated with two sulfur and two oxygen atoms are anchored on the surface of PMA2PbI4 via a W-O-Pb link. The resulting WADCs-decorated PMA2PbI4 (WADCs/S-PMA2PbI4) exhibits an extraordinary interfacial charge transfer efficiency of 94.7%, which is much higher than that of Pt/PMA2PbI4 (61.7%). Moreover, WADCs can effectively extend the lifetime of hot carriers and work as the active sites for HER. Consequently, WADCs/S-PMA2PbI4 shows a photocatalytic HER activity superior to that of Pt/PMA2PbI4 and 30 times that of bare PMA2PbI4 with a record turnover frequency (TOF) of 516.3 h-1 per W atom. This work opens a new avenue for designing cost-effective perovskite-based catalysts for solar hydrogen production. title: Data-augmented machine learning for predicting biomass-derived hard carbon anode performance in sodium-ion batteries
Diverse local environments in Ru,Ir-Nb2O5 enable enhanced oxygen evolution in acidic media
abstract: Ru- and Ir-based oxides are benchmarks for the acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER), but are too costly for large-scale deployment. Doping Ru or Ir into acid-stable supports offers a promising route to reduce noble-metal usage. Herein, we utilized the complex structural landscape of Nb 2 O 5 to design catalysts with enhanced performance. This was achieved by combining computational screening with interpretable machine learning (ML) to systematically probe diverse local environments across crystalline and amorphous Ru- and Ir-doped Nb 2 O 5 . Our predictions showed that Ru- and Ir-doped R- and M-Nb 2 O 5 exhibited lower theoretical overpotentials than the RuO 2 and IrO 2 benchmarks. Analysis of local environments indicated that higher oxygen coordination around the noble metal is beneficial for activity. The ML model identified the oxygen 2 p band center as the primary activity descriptor, complemented by local geometric distortions. Guided by these insights, the predicted catalysts were synthesized, achieving activity and stability superior to the RuO 2 and IrO 2 benchmarks. This work provides a general framework for rationally designing high-performance, cost-effective electrocatalysts by exploiting the tunability of local environments.

Biomass chemical looping: A sustainable pathway for energy and chemicals
abstract: Biomass valorisations in efficient and sustainable ways are widely considered as practical approaches for simultaneously mitigating climate change and strengthening energy security. Compared to conventional thermochemical and biochemical biomass valorisation approaches, biomass chemical looping (BCL) has attracted attention, owing to its advantages of high energy efficiency, controllable main products, and high-purity CO 2 separation by a simple condensation unit. In this review, we discuss BCL technical routes in terms of targeted products and practical applications, providing underlying mechanisms and optimization methodologies to reduce energy consumption and improve conversion efficiency with high-purity desired products. As one typical data-driven approach, machine learning (ML) is an emerging approach for accurate design of oxygen carriers and efficient optimisation of reduction-oxidation cycles, significantly enhancing large-scale applications of BCL technologies. Moreover, we address environmental impacts and economic feasibility of typical BCL approaches for providing comprehensive guidelines to researchers, industrial practitioners, and policymakers. Owing to the excellent environmental and economic benefits of BCL-to-H 2 for green methanol production, we highlight its potential as a multifunctional alternative to conventional power generation and biowaste management technologies. With concerted efforts, sustainable BCL for value-added products such as green electricity, hydrogen, and methanol is beneficial to achieving UN SDGs 7, 12, and 13.

title: Differentiable hybrid force fields support scalable autonomous electrolyte discovery
abstract: Autonomous electrolyte discovery demands a computational engine that satisfies a critical trilemma: it must be fast enough for high-throughput screening, accurate enough for quantitative property prediction, and calibratable enough for online refinement. Classical empirical force fields (FFs) are fast but rely on error cancellation, while standard machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) are computationally expensive. In this Perspective, we highlight that differentiable hybrid FFs resolve this trilemma by fusing physically motivated functional forms with neural-network short-range corrections. Grounded in Energy Decomposition Analysis (EDA), state-of-the-art models such as PhyNEO-Electrolyte and ByteFF-Pol achieve zero-shot generalization to bulk phases, delivering throughputs on the order of tens of ns/day (up to $\sim$50 ns/day, depending on model complexity) for 10,000-atom systems. Crucially, their physical skeletons provide a well-conditioned parameter space for differentiable molecular dynamics (dMD). This enables a dual-calibration paradigm: bottom-up \textit{ab initio} parameterization combined with top-down fine-tuning from macroscopic experimental observables. We propose that this architecture meets the requirements of a ``ChemRobot-ready'' digital twin by integrating physics-grounded simulation with experimentally calibratable refinement, thereby enabling closed-loop autonomous electrolyte discovery.

Unlocking rechargeable battery materials with artificial intelligence: From data-descriptor-model workflows to closed-loop discovery
abstract: Faced with the vast chemical space of materials, traditional trial-and-error approaches have become increasingly inadequate for rechargeable battery development because of long development cycles, high costs, and limited screening efficiency. Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly machine learning, has been applied to extract relationships among composition, structure, processing conditions, and material properties from computational and experimental data. These models support rapid property prediction, screening of large candidate spaces, and iterative selection of informative experiments. This review focuses on lithium-ion, sodium-ion, and zinc-ion batteries and provides an overview of the key technologies, application progress, challenges, and future directions of AI-driven rechargeable battery development. The technical foundations and general workflow are first outlined. Recent advances in AI applications to cathodes, anodes, liquid electrolytes, and solid-state electrolytes are then reviewed, with emphasis on high-throughput screening, performance prediction, and structure-property relationship mining. Current challenges are further analyzed in terms of data quality, descriptor construction, interpretability, and generalization capability. Future directions, including novel descriptor systems, AI-enhanced characterization, inverse design, and closed-loop development enabled by robotic automation and large language models, are also discussed in relation to intelligent battery research. This review is intended to provide a theoretical reference for the accelerated discovery of next-generation rechargeable battery chemistries and key materials.

title: Machine learning-assisted health management of retired batteries
Artificial intelligence for perovskite solar cells and light-emitting diodes: from machine learning to large language models
Single-atom collaboration with cluster for accelerated nitrate electroreduction: Synergy revelation via machine learning and DFT calculations
abstract: Exploring high-performance electrocatalysts for the nitrate reduction reaction (NO3RR) is crucial for environmental nitrate removal and ammonia synthesis. Single-atom collaboration with cluster can provide sufficient active sites for catalysts to promote NO3RR, yet the unclear synergistic effect between the two hinders their rational design. Herein, a series of Ir3 clusters and metal single atoms co-embedded in graphitic carbon nitride (g-CN) catalysts (Ir3M1) were constructed, and the synergistic effects of Ir3 clusters and M1 single atoms on the NO3RR catalytic mechanism and activity were systematically explored using density functional theory (DFT) calculations combined with machine learning. Comprehensive evaluations of structural stability and catalytic activity demonstrate that the synergy between single atoms and clusters effectively balances the adsorption energies of key intermediates, yielding exceptional catalytic performance (the limiting potential of Ir3Ti1 can reach −0.22 V). Machine learning models further clarify the synergistic mechanism, where the geometric configurations of clusters serve as critical features for modulating the catalytic activity of single-atom sites, whereas the electronic structures of single atoms directly govern the reactivity of cluster sites. This DFT-machine learning approach provides theoretical guidelines for catalyst design and a predictive framework for efficient NO3RR electrocatalysts.

title: Machine learning-inspired process-based models for adsorption selectivity between CO2 and CH4 on coal
abstract: Adsorption selectivity of gases on porous substrates is a fundamental challenge in both materials science and applied engineering. Traditional models derived from single-component data and limited observations are insufficient to capture the integrated effects of temperature, pressure, and gas composition that govern multicomponent competitive sorption. We address this challenge by collecting then utilizing an ensemble data suite comprising 1017 entries for 43 coal samples under diverse conditions for CO2/CH4 competitive adsorption. This dataset was used to train four machine learning models to predict adsorption selectivity, among which XGBoost achieved the best performance. This ML-based model achieves a 14.6% improvement over traditional numerical models. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis was performed to investigate the individual and interaction effects of key factors on adsorption selectivity. Pressure exhibits a non-monotonic three-stage influence on selectivity, governed sequentially by energetic, entropic, and pore-network effects. Coal rank, gas composition, and pressure exhibit pronounced interactions that reshape their individual contributions. Temperature suppresses CO2 competitiveness, especially at low CO2 fractions, due to its higher adsorption heat and enhanced thermal motion. This study establishes a data-driven framework integrating ML and adsorption physics for elucidating competitive adsorption in multicomponent gas systems, thereby advancing interdisciplinary inquiry across materials science, carbon sequestration, and natural gas development.

title: Flame-retardant bimodal wrinkled strain sensor for deep learning-assisted gesture recognition and human-machine interaction
abstract: Resistive fabric-based strain sensors show great potential in wearable electronics; however, their practical applications remain limited by the intrinsic trade-off between high sensitivity and a wide strain range, as well as the inherent flammability of the fabric substrate, which poses potential safety risks under high-temperature or fire conditions. To address this issue, a flame-retardant flexible strain sensor based on a MXene/CNTs bimodal wrinkled structure was rationally designed according to a three-step procedure as follows: (i) constructing a MXene/CNTs conductive network through Ti–O–C covalent bonds, (ii) generating a bimodal wrinkled structure by swelling-deswelling-induced interfacial buckling of the thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) substrate, and (iii) integrating a biomass-derived phytic acid coating to impart flame retardancy. Benefiting from the dynamic reconfiguration of Ti–O–C bonds and the variation in wrinkles across layers during the stretching process, the sensor exhibits high sensitivity (gauge factor = 4851.23), a wide strain detection range (0%–190%), and excellent long-term stability through 10,000 cycles. Moreover, the sensor integrates passive-active fire safety, raising the membrane char residue to 40.3% at 800 °C to inhibit molten droplets and achieve self-extinguishing, while also enabling rapid high-temperature alarm triggering. As a proof-of-concept application, a wearable human-machine interaction system enables wireless gesture control and fire warning, achieving a recognition accuracy of 99.33% for five gesture commands with the assistance of deep learning. This work provides an effective strategy for integrating high-performance strain sensing with active-passive synergistic flame retardancy, offering valuable guidance for intelligent wearable electronics and safety-monitoring systems.

title: A machine learning framework for biorefinery pretreatment design
abstract: Lignocellulosic biorefineries are essential to the circular economy but are limited by biomass recalcitrance and the high cost of pretreatment optimization. Existing machine-learning approaches are typically restricted to single feedstocks or processes, largely due to fragmented and inconsistent data. Here we present LAM-Pre, a framework that integrates large language model (LLM)-assisted literature mining, systematic machine-learning benchmarking, and experimental validation to predict glucose yields across diverse pretreatment and enzymatic hydrolysis conditions. Using ChatGPT-assisted data extraction, we curated a comprehensive Pret-Glucose dataset spanning multiple biomass types, pretreatment strategies, and enzymes. Benchmarking 16 supervised models identified Gradient Boosting Decision Trees (GBDT) as the best-performing model within the current heterogeneous dataset. Experimental validation demonstrated strong trend-level consistency (up to PCC = 0.9) of glucose yields across diverse and mixed biomass feedstocks. Virtual screening of 1,092,000 process-condition combinations enabled rapid identification of high-yield regimes, including a sodium hydroxide-hydrogen peroxide pretreatment achieving 96% glucose yield. LAM-Pre was further applied to mixed biomass systems, experimentally delivering up to a 34.8% yield increase over single-feedstock processing. LAM-Pre establishes a scalable, data-driven workflow for flexible and economically viable biorefinery design.

title: Synthesis-driven discovery of high-performance fuels using ultra-high precision graph neural networks
abstract: Efforts to accelerate the development of high-performance hydrocarbon fuels with high energy density for advanced aerospace propulsion are frequently hindered by the synthetic infeasibility of designed molecules. Here, we present a molecular design framework that generates high-performance hydrocarbon fuels while explicitly defining their synthetic feedstocks and routes. Using cyclopropanation and hydrogenation reactions as templates, we design 1000 synthesizable accessibility hydrocarbons. To enable rapid and accurate property evaluation, we develop graph neural networks (GNN) models that integrate attention mechanisms and multi-order convolutional edges. These models are trained on a manually curated dataset of 2068 hydrocarbons with over 11,000 data points for density (ρ), net heat of combustion (NHOC), viscosity (η), boiling point (Tb), and melting point (Tm). The optimal models achieve prediction accuracy of 0.998, 0.997, 0.998, 0.919, and 0.996 for ρ, NHOC, Tb, Tm, and η, respectively. Predictions indicate that 174 of the designed hydrocarbons surpass the energy density of the benchmark fuel JP-10 (39.40 MJ/L), with a maximum of 46.62 MJ/L. Six of these hydrocarbons are synthesized, and the experimental values are in strong agreement with the predicted values. This result validates both the synthetic feasibility of the designed molecules and the superior predictive performance of the GNN models. This synthesis-driven design paradigm accelerates the discovery of next-generation aerospace fuels and is extendable to other small-molecule design tasks.

title: Decoding diverse pressure–composition–temperature behavior of hydrogen storage alloys via physics-constrained machine learning
abstract: Pressure–composition–temperature (PCT) curves provide a fundamental basis for evaluating the hydrogen absorption and desorption behavior of hydrogen storage alloys. Different hydrogen storage mechanisms give rise to distinct PCT curve types, and variations in factors such as alloy composition, phase constitution, and measurement conditions further increase their complexity, making unified prediction and interpretation challenging. In this paper, a physics-constrained machine-learning framework was developed by integrating a monotonicity penalty, isotonic regression, and transfer learning. Multi-principal element alloys (MPEAs), Mg–Ni–RE (RE = La and Y) alloys, and V–Ti–Cr alloys were selected as representative systems for single-plateau, dual-plateau, and cyclic PCT curves, respectively. The resulting models accurately reproduced experimental PCT behavior, and their predictive performance for MPEAs and Mg–Ni–RE alloys was further evaluated using experimental data not used in model construction. Thermodynamic and hydrogen storage parameters were subsequently derived from the predicted curves. Key factors associated with reversible capacity in MPEAs, MgH2 thermodynamic stability in Mg–Ni–RE alloys, and cycling stability in V–Ti–Cr alloys were identified, providing theoretical guidance for tailoring these properties. The framework could be extended to model hydrogen absorption/desorption kinetic curves and their evolution during cycling, supporting multi-objective optimization of hydrogen storage performance.

title: A multi-scale temporal fusion network for accurate and uncertainty-aware battery remaining useful life prediction
abstract: Accurate prediction of the remaining useful life (RUL) of lithium-ion batteries requires the concurrent satisfaction of three technical demands: efficient modeling of long sequences, fusion of multi-scale features, and reliable quantification of prediction uncertainty. This study proposes MSTFNet, a multi-scale temporal fusion network that integrates a spatial convolutional neural network (SCNN) for local patterns, a Mamba state-space module for linear-time modeling of global dependencies, and an Informer module for sparse temporal focusing, all under a Bayesian inference head optimized via a combined negative log-likelihood and mean-squared-error objective. The Bayesian head not only calibrates uncertainty but also regulates multi-module feature fusion, achieving a cooperative synergy unavailable to single modules alone. Across three benchmark datasets (NASA, CALCE, and HUST), MSTFNet attains a superior balance between prediction accuracy and model efficiency, achieving up to 29.4 % lower RMSE than state-of-the-art baselines. Further analyses confirm well-calibrated predictive intervals, robust cross-dataset generalization under train-on-A/test-on-B and few-shot settings, and deployment feasibility in terms of latency, memory, and INT8/pruning performance. Ablation results substantiate that BNN-regulated joint optimization effectively enhances Informer collaboration, validating the proposed regulatory mechanism.

title: Scalable one-pot regeneration of spent LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 into high-performance SiO2-coated single-crystal cathodes via data-driven optimization
abstract: Direct regeneration offers a highly feasible route for recycling spent lithium-ion batteries by reducing process complexity and transportation burdens. However, regenerated cathodes often fail to fully recover their original electrochemical performance due to persistent surface degradation. Herein, we report a scalable one-pot strategy to directly regenerate spent LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 (NCM) into single-crystal NCM coated with a thin SiO2 protective layer (SC-NCM@SiO2). In this process, a uniform and robust SiO2 coating is formed during the conventional washing step using an aqueous silane coupling agent solution, eliminating the need for additional surface modification procedures. A data-driven optimization approach based on Gaussian-process-based Bayesian optimization was employed to determine the optimal silane concentration for maximizing electrochemical performance. The resulting SC-NCM@SiO2 cathode delivers a high reversible capacity of 207.8 mA h g−1 and exhibits excellent cycling stability with 82% capacity retention and 99.99% Coulombic efficiency after 800 cycles in full cells. Furthermore, the regeneration process is successfully demonstrated at the kilogram scale, highlighting its compatibility with industrial manufacturing. This work provides a practical pathway toward scalable and commercially viable regeneration of high-performance Ni-rich cathodes.

title: An interpretable adaptive framework for cross-domain state of health prediction in lithium-ion batteries
abstract: The data domain shift encountered across diverse operating conditions and disparate material systems constitutes a critical bottleneck, substantially hindering the generalization capability of state-of-health (SOH) prediction models for lithium-ion batteries (LIBs). Furthermore, existing data-driven transfer learning methods exhibit pronounced “black-box” characteristics during the cross-domain adaptation phase, resulting in a profound lack of interpretability regarding their decision-making mechanisms. To circumvent these limitations, this study proposes an efficient and interpretable transfer learning framework tailored for cross-domain scenarios. By incorporating SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) attribution analysis, the framework effectively alleviates the opacity inherent in model transfer. Specifically, the high consistency observed in the feature importance distribution under multi-rate conditions for identical materials demonstrates that the model successfully mitigates the interference of dynamic operations, stably anchoring the common underlying degradation laws. Conversely, across distinct material systems, the significant reconstruction of feature weights intuitively reflects the model capability to perceive and adapt to shifts in dominant aging modes. Ultimately, this research offers a novel perspective on bridging the gap between data-driven “black-box” models and the underlying electrochemical aging mechanisms.

title: A dual-level interpretability method for state of health estimation integrating mechanism-related insights in lithium-ion batteries
abstract: Accurate state of health (SOH) estimation is essential for battery management. However, the limited interpretability of data-driven models constrains their deployment, since prediction accuracy alone is often insufficient to ensure physical consistency. To address this, this study proposes a dual-level interpretable method integrating adaptive feature engineering with model interpretability analysis. Specifically, at the feature interpretation level, K-means clustering adaptively identifies aging trends and partitions voltage intervals from constant current charging curves to extract interpretable electrochemical-related features. Following recursive feature elimination, a random forest algorithm is employed to estimate SOH. Experiments on multi-chemistry public datasets and real-world electric vehicle data validate stable accuracy and robustness. Furthermore, regarding model interpretation, a static-dynamic framework integrating Shapley additive explanations with generalized additive models is established. This analysis reveals chemical-dependent feature variations and identifies non-linear patterns involving threshold and saturation effects in feature responses. Crucially, these findings empirically associate feature variations with mechanism-related degradation patterns, thereby providing a quantitative perspective for mechanistically informed analysis. Ultimately, incorporating interpretability into both feature extraction and decision-making elevates estimation transparency and credibility.

title: Feature-augmented machine-learning guided insights into cationic groups and alkaline-resistant mechanism of anion exchange membranes for water electrolysis
abstract: The alkaline stability of cationic groups for anion exchange membranes (AEMs) severely hinders the development of AEM water electrolysis for large-scale green hydrogen production. However, it is time-consuming and laborious to study cationic groups by traditionally empirical methods. Here, a feature-augmented machine-learning (ML) model is firstly applied in ML-AEM framework to design cationic groups with the degradation rate lower than 0.1% under alkaline concentration of 1 M, temperature of 80 °C, and time of 720 h. Eight cationic groups are effectively selected from 260,040 candidates, by high-throughput screening and LUMO energy level analysis. Some important features of the selected cationic groups are revealed in terms of electronic and geometric structure, by local and global SHAP analysis. A new phosphonium cationic group is discovered and further synthesized, which shows the superior alkaline stability with no degradation after 1000 h in extremely high alkaline solutions (i.e., 13.65 M NaODaq). Besides, density functional theory calculations inspired by SHAP analysis results are used to analyze the influence of electronic and geometric features on alkaline stability of the cationic groups, showing trends generally consistent with SHAP-derived interpretations. Finally, the AEM synthesized based on the screening results also demonstrates promising performance in anion exchange membrane water electrolysis. Overall, it provides a promising way to small-molecule cation screening for AEM-related stability studies.
